pages.text: Sealed-cavity matrices enclose scattered machines in a hollow box and merge them into one machine.$(br2)$(bold)Universal rules:$(reset)$(li)The casing forms a hollow sealed box with an odd edge length (3 or 5)$(li)Casings form the walls; ports and the controller are mounted on them, and the cavity must be empty$(li)Once formed it operates as one unit; breaking any casing block immediately disables it$(br2)In addition to the generator and purifier matrices there is a third: the Miniature Matrix Terminal. It uses the same sealed cavity, but its cavity accepts upgrade components and its walls accept Miniature Terminal chips, allowing it to schedule machines across the air. The individual entries provide exact layouts and stats.

$(bold)Generator Matrix (power):$(reset) encloses the Energy Generator in a sealed cavity and burns fuel at a fixed multiplier. Two tiers exist: Basic 3×3×3 and Advanced 5×5×5; formed-structure stats and fuel/energy port connections are in the $(l:akaishi:gen_matrix)Akaishi Generator Matrix$(/l) entry.$(br2)$(bold)Purifier Matrix (refining):$(reset) a 3×3×3 cavity converted into a central refining line that processes raw blocks and crystal blocks into essence in bulk at 30x speed. It runs on grid power and has no fuel slot; see the $(l:akaishi:purifier_matrix)Purifier Matrix$(/l) entry.$(br2)Both follow the rules above; reading this overview first keeps the layout clear.

Matrices are derived from single-block machines: the $(l:akaishi:generator)Energy Generator$(/l) and the $(l:akaishi:purifier)Akaishi Purifier$(/l) each have their own entry, and the two matrices are built from them. The third form is the $(l:akaishi:mini_matrix)Miniature Matrix Terminal$(/l): chips on the walls of a 5x5x5 cavity network it and schedule machines across the air.
